import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_21/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_21/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# UNION the two sources (schemas are the same)
df_union = pd.concat([df0, df1], ignore_index=True)

# Convert draw_sales to numeric, coerce errors to NaN, then fill NaN with 0
df_union['draw_sales'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['draw_sales'], errors='coerce').fillna(0)

# Extract year from date column (date format is YYYY-MM-DD)
df_union['year'] = pd.to_datetime(df_union['date'], errors='coerce').dt.year

# Group by state and date, sum draw_sales
df_grouped = df_union.groupby(['state', 'date'], as_index=False).agg({'draw_sales': 'sum'})

# After grouping, year is ambiguous because multiple rows with same state+date could have different years,
# but date is unique per row, so year can be extracted from date again.
df_grouped['year'] = pd.to_datetime(df_grouped['date'], errors='coerce').dt.year

# Ensure types match target schema:
# 'state': string
df_grouped['state'] = df_grouped['state'].astype(str)
# 'date': string (keep as YYYY-MM-DD)
df_grouped['date'] = df_grouped['date'].astype(str)
# 'draw_sales': integer (convert safely)
df_grouped['draw_sales'] = df_grouped['draw_sales'].round(0).astype(int)
# 'year': integer
df_grouped['year'] = df_grouped['year'].astype(int)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_df = df_grouped[['state', 'date', 'draw_sales', 'year']]

# Write to target path without index
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_21/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
